title: ScreenDx identifies previously underdetected interstitial lung disease in COPDGene scans
summary: A retrospective COPDGene analysis used a learned CT model to detect cases subsequently relabeled as clinically significant interstitial lung disease. The original abstract reports 84.8% sensitivity and 98.0% specificity in a deliberately sampled cohort. This does not establish prospective screening benefit.
organization: Stanford University; IMVARIA; University of North Carolina; University of Utah; University of Alabama at Birmingham

evidence.tested: The source selected patients subsequently relabeled by COPDGene investigators as ILD-positive and sampled COPD/control negatives to target approximately 1–2% ILD prevalence. At a previously selected threshold, abstract-reported sensitivity was 84.8%(95% CI 68.1–94.9%) and specificity 98.0%(97.3–98.5%).
evidence.unknown: This review had the complete original abstract and primary bibliographic metadata, not full Methods. Exact sample counts, details of clinical adjudication, model-development overlap and threshold-lock timing were not authenticated. Positives had already been relabeled by investigators; these are not newly confirmed diagnoses made in a prospective AI screening program. Deliberate negative sampling limits prevalence-dependent interpretation. No improved patient outcomes or causal clinical benefit is established. The original journal history gives online publication November 26,2025, while PubMed records November 27; the represented date follows the original publisher.
evidence.ai_role: A learned ScreenDx model evaluates CT features compatible with ILD; this is a retrospective test against subsequently assigned clinical reference labels.

source_review.scope: Complete original PubMed/EuropePMC abstract plus indexed original journal abstract and original publisher publication history actually read; full Methods unavailable (journal403).
